key_insight: Deep generative crystal structure prediction models perform well, but most of their successes overlap with template-based retrieval, showing they are not yet truly de novo predictors.
engineering_relevance: For materials discovery pipelines, the practical value of generative CSP lies less in raw accuracy and more in expanding beyond existing prototype libraries.
method: Benchmarked 12 representative generative CSP models across latent-variable, diffusion, flow-matching, autoregressive, and manifold random-walk families.
Used identical structure-matching, symmetry, and consensus criteria against TCSP 2.0 for fair comparison.
Performed a controlled prototype-removal retraining test to measure dependence on known structural families.
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 180 test structures, with a leakage-controlled subset of 46, and found template retrieval at 68.3% top-1 success versus 66.4% for EquiCSP and 62.9% for Uni-3DAR.
watch_item: Reported gains may overstate true novelty because many predictions depend strongly on prototype families seen during training, and performance dropped 50–78% when four families were removed.
paper_title: Deep Generative Crystal Structure Prediction: A Benchmark Study and a Controlled Test of Prototype Dependence
